title: Window pegs: Proof strip
summary: Monotonic deques. Return the whole result list in the order you built it.
descriptionMd:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
readings is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless Step 1 says otherwise. k is a whole number. Use it as described in the steps below.

Step 1: Build the result list
Take every group of exactly k numbers next to each other in readings. Move the group one place right each time. Record the largest number in each group, from left to right. If k is larger than the input length, the result list is empty.

Step 2: Return the answer
Return the whole result list in the order you built it. If it is empty, return [].

Write your function
Complete windowPegsProofStrip(readings, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.
unitIntro: Take every group of exactly k numbers next to each other in readings. Move the group one place right each time. Record the largest number in each group, from left to right. If k is larger than the input length, the result list is empty. Each card first builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.
constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in Step 1.
Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the result list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
